title: Many Ways to Break the Same Number
objective: Systematically find all the whole-number ways to split a given small quantity, not just one or two.
studentQuestion: Have you found every way, or might there be more?
newIdea: Exhaustive (systematic) search for decompositions, not just a few examples.

teaching.see: How many different ways do you think 7 can be broken into two parts?
teaching.break: Search systematically — start from one part being 1, then 2, then 3, and so on.
teaching.build: Record each pair found (1&6, 2&5, 3&4) and notice when pairs start repeating in reverse.
teaching.transform: The same whole (7), organized as a complete, ordered list of forms.

check.prompt: Count the total number of distinct splits found and justify none were missed or duplicated.

examples.transfer: 9, found independently by the learner using the same systematic method.

mastery.evidence: Finds at least 3 distinct splits of 7 (or 6) using a systematic method, not trial and error.
